articles.title: Longpoint Partners Buys Miami-Dade Warehouses for $39M
articles.narrative: Longpoint Partners has acquired a three-warehouse industrial complex in Miami-Dade County for $38.8 million. The fully leased small-bay warehouses, totaling 121,579 square feet across two addresses in Medley, were sold by Martha and Ruben Artiles, who had owned the properties since the 1980s and 1990s. This acquisition continues Longpoint Partners' active investment strategy in the South Florida industrial market.

data_points.notable_features: Small-bay warehouses located about half a mile west of the Palmetto Expressway.

articles.title: Affinius Capital Provides $188M Refi for N.J. Mixed-Use Apartment Complex
articles.narrative: A joint venture comprising PCCP, Claremont Development, and Stanbery Development Group has secured a $188 million refinancing package for District 15Fifteen, a newly opened 498-unit mixed-use multifamily property in Parsippany, NJ. Affinius Capital provided the debt, which will support the lease-up and stabilization of the asset. The property is considered a high-quality asset in a supply-constrained, transit-oriented submarket with compelling fundamentals.

data_points.notable_features: Mixed-use property with three buildings, including 58,800 square feet of retail space and an 853-space parking garage. Amenities include a fitness center, multiple courtyards, a pool, a roof deck, and a dog spa.
data_points.project_notes: The property opened in June 2026.

articles.title: PwC’s Move to Century City Is Another Blow to Downtown L.A.
articles.narrative: PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) is relocating its Los Angeles office from Downtown L.A. to Century City, signing a 15-year lease for approximately 150,000 square feet at 2121 Avenue of the Stars. The move, valued at roughly $200 million, is driven by PwC's need for additional space and improved accessibility to transportation and airports. This relocation is another significant blow to Downtown L.A.'s office market, which has seen several major tenants depart in recent years, while Century City continues to attract high-profile firms with its premier amenities and strong market performance.

data_points.address: 2121 Avenue of the Stars, Los Angeles, CA
data_points.notable_features: Features unmatched amenities and strong access to transportation corridors and airports.
data_points.project_notes: PwC will vacate 114,000 square feet at 601 South Figueroa Street in Downtown L.A. when its current lease expires in 2028. The 15-year lease is reportedly valued at approximately $200 million.

articles.market_intelligence: Greater L.A. recorded nearly 4 million square feet of office leasing during Q2, a 15% increase from the prior quarter and 8% above the same period last year, exceeding the market’s five-year quarterly average by 22%. Century City commanded the region’s highest average asking rents in Q2 at $7.67 per square foot per month, compared to Beverly Hills at $6.71 per square foot. Downtown L.A.'s overall office vacancy has climbed 20 percentage points since 2019, with almost 40% of financial district office space available for lease at the end of 2025.

articles.title: Manufacturing, Big-Box Leasing Fuel U.S. Industrial Reset in 2026
articles.narrative: The U.S. industrial market is experiencing a significant reset in 2026, driven by robust leasing activity, particularly for large spaces, and a diversifying demand base fueled by a new wave of manufacturing investment. National asking rents have risen despite elevated vacancy, while new construction has moderated from pandemic-era highs. This shift is characterized by substantial manufacturing job announcements and capital investment, with a notable focus on aerospace, defense, AI infrastructure, energy equipment, and pharmaceuticals, rather than solely electric vehicles.
articles.market_intelligence: National vacancy rate finished Q2 2026 at 8.2%, unchanged from Q1 and 10 basis points higher than a year ago. Industrial construction pipeline is 320 million square feet, less than half the 782 million-square-foot peak in late 2022. Deliveries dropped to 49.4 million square feet during Q2 2026 from over 82 million square feet at this point last year. Southern California remains the top market due to its port complex. North Carolina, Texas, and California led the nation in announced manufacturing jobs.

articles.title: Bravo Property Trust Lends $68M on New Jersey Waterfront Apartments
articles.narrative: Skyrock Capital secured $68 million in construction financing from Bravo Property Trust for its 180-unit luxury waterfront multifamily project in Bayonne, NJ. The development, known as Bayonne Luxury Waterwalk, is situated on a 2.3-acre site along Newark Bay. A Bravo Property Trust executive noted that Bayonne's waterfront is drawing significant long-term investment, and the lender was pleased to provide the necessary financing certainty for the sponsor to proceed with construction.

data_points.notable_features: Luxury waterfront property along Newark Bay with a swimming pool and fitness center.
data_points.project_notes: The 2.3-acre site was previously acquired for $4.55 million in 2019. Two floors of the six-story building will be used for parking.

articles.title: NRP Group Breaks Ground on 348-Unit Affordable Housing Project in South Austin
articles.narrative: The NRP Group, in partnership with the Housing Authority of Travis County, has broken ground on Sanara, a 348-unit affordable housing project in South Austin. The development will feature 13 three-story residential buildings with units restricted to renters earning 60 percent or less of the area median income. MetLife Investment Management is the tax credit investor, and PIMCO provided construction and permanent financing for the project.

data_points.notable_features: Units will be rent restricted to renters earning 60 percent or less of the area median income; amenities include a fitness center, business center, clubhouse, outdoor pool, children's activity center, and playground.
data_points.project_notes: Residents will have access to services such as afterschool care, financial literacy courses, ESL classes, and first-time homebuyer programs.

articles.title: IPA Arranges Sale of 250-Unit Alta Firewheel Apartments in Garland, Texas
articles.narrative: Institutional Property Advisors (IPA) has facilitated the sale of Alta Firewheel, a 250-unit apartment complex in Garland, Texas. Wood Partners, based in Atlanta, sold the property to Pardue Cos. The transaction involved a recently constructed asset, completed in 2024, offering a range of unit types and modern amenities.

data_points.notable_features: Amenities include a pool, fitness center, lounge, game room, coffee bar, and outdoor grilling and dining stations.

articles.title: Avison Young Negotiates 61,861 SF Industrial Lease in Grand Prairie, Texas
articles.narrative: Avison Young has brokered a 10-year industrial lease for 61,861 square feet in Grand Prairie, Texas. The tenant, Flow Control Group, will occupy space within Building 2 of the industrial property at 3550 N. Highway 161. The transaction highlights continued demand for industrial space in the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex.

data_points.project_notes: 10-year lease term.

articles.title: Pye-Barker Fire & Safety Signs 13,776 SF Industrial Lease in Irving
articles.narrative: Pye-Barker Fire & Safety LLC has signed a 13,776-square-foot industrial lease at Skyway Corporate Center in Irving, Texas. The company, which provides alarm and monitoring systems, was represented by CBRE, while Bradford Commercial Real Estate Services represented the landlord.

articles.title: Newmark Arranges $515M Refinancing of Midtown Manhattan Office Building
articles.narrative: Newmark has arranged a substantial $515 million refinancing package for 31 West 52nd Street, a prominent 785,000-square-foot office building in Midtown Manhattan. The debt, secured by local investment firm Rithm Capital, comprises a $415 million senior mortgage, a $40 million B-note, and a $60 million mezzanine loan. A consortium of major financial institutions, led by Wells Fargo, provided the financing.

data_points.address: 31 West 52nd Street, New York City, NY
data_points.project_notes: The debt package includes a $415 million senior mortgage loan, a $40 million B-note, and a $60 million mezzanine loan.

articles.title: Close to Home: How Chicago’s neighborhood retail corridors are outrunning Downtown
articles.narrative: Chicago's neighborhood retail corridors are outperforming downtown retail due to a sustained shift in consumer behavior towards local spending and working closer to home. This has led to increased and more consistent foot traffic in areas like Armitage and Southport, making them attractive to retailers, including national brands seeking predictable customer bases. The limited supply of quality retail space in these desirable neighborhood markets, driven by factors like high replacement costs and entrenched ownership, is supporting rent growth and landlord leverage. While downtown areas like the Magnificent Mile are seeing some renewed interest in experiential concepts, their recovery is hampered by the inconsistency of hybrid work schedules, making neighborhood locations more appealing for retailers dependent on steady daily activity.

articles.title: CBRE arranges sale of 28,150-square-foot redevelopment site in Chicago’s Wrigleyville submarket
articles.narrative: A joint venture between SNS Realty Group and North Park Ventures has acquired a 28,150-square-foot redevelopment site in Chicago's Wrigleyville submarket for $6.25 million. The buyers successfully secured a zoning change to B2-5, enabling the development of a five-story, 99-unit apartment building. The property, formerly home to a glass manufacturing company, is strategically located near Wrigley Field and a CTA station, an area experiencing significant residential growth.

data_points.notable_features: Site is located in the Wrigleyville submarket of Lakeview, near Wrigley Field and the CTA's Belmont station.
data_points.project_notes: The site was previously home to Torstenson Glass Company for over 60 years. Buyers secured a zoning change to B2-5 for the planned development.

articles.title: Marcus & Millichap closes sale of mixed-use property in Tinley Park
articles.narrative: Marcus & Millichap has brokered the sale of Boulevard at Central Station, a recently built mixed-use property in Tinley Park, IL. The asset, featuring 66 multifamily units and five ground-floor retail spaces, was marketed exclusively by Marcus & Millichap, which also procured the buyer. The property's prime location across from Harmony Square and the Tinley Park Metra Station offers residents convenient access to downtown Chicago.

data_points.notable_features: Amenities include a clubhouse, fitness studio, yoga room, smart home technology, an outdoor lounge, and a dog wash. Located directly across from Harmony Square and the Tinley Park Metra Station.

articles.title: Marcus & Millichap negotiates sale of Public Storage property in Chicago
articles.narrative: Marcus & Millichap has brokered the sale of a newly constructed Public Storage facility in Chicago, featuring 916 climate-controlled self-storage units. The property, completed in 2024, was sold by an Illinois-based LLC to a Texas-based LLC. The transaction highlights continued investor interest in institutional-quality self-storage assets located in densely populated urban areas.

data_points.notable_features: Climate-controlled units, strong visibility along North Kedzie Avenue, located in a densely populated area with a predominantly renter-occupied housing base.

articles.title: Thrive Senior Living buys land for senior living development in Ooltewah
articles.narrative: Thrive Senior Living has acquired an 80-acre parcel in Ooltewah, Tennessee, for a new senior living development. The project will feature approximately 400 units across a full continuum of care, including 55+ single-family homes, independent living cottages and apartments, assisted living, and memory care. The development aims to provide a hospitality-driven lifestyle within a residential-scale environment, offering strong amenities and diverse living options to meet evolving resident needs.

data_points.notable_features: Located within a growth corridor with access to retail, healthcare, churches, residential neighborhoods, and regional transportation routes.
data_points.project_notes: The single-family homes within the development will be built by RP Communities.

articles.title: Lincoln Property pays $61M for office campus in Boston suburb
articles.narrative: Lincoln Property Company, in partnership with an investor group advised by JPMorgan Asset Management, has acquired The Edge office campus in Wakefield, MA, for $61 million. The seven-building, 962,000-square-foot complex was sold by Hobbs Brook Real Estate, which developed the campus on the former Pleasure Island amusement park site. Lincoln Property sees significant value-add and mixed-use redevelopment potential in the property, which is located approximately 12 miles north of Downtown Boston.

data_points.notable_features: Seven-building office campus located on the former Pleasure Island amusement park site, approximately 12 miles north of Downtown Boston.
data_points.project_notes: Hobbs Brook Real Estate assembled and developed the office park between 2001 and 2011. Hobbs Brook announced capital improvements at 601 and 701 Edgewater Drive in 2024, including café renovation, fitness center improvements, and a new conference center.

articles.title: Centerspace takes 48% hit on Denver apartment sale to Four Peaks
articles.narrative: Centerspace Homes sold the Civic Lofts apartment building in Denver's Golden Triangle for $30 million to an LLC linked to Four Peaks Multifamily Partners. This sale represents a 48% discount from its 2021 purchase price of $63 million and is part of Centerspace's strategy to divest $240-$245 million in properties to reduce debt. The acquisition marks Four Peaks Multifamily Partners' entry into the Denver city market.

data_points.notable_features: 14-story building located in the Golden Triangle submarket.
data_points.project_notes: Property was previously acquired by Centerspace in 2021 for $63 million.

articles.market_intelligence: Denver's Golden Triangle submarket has seen units delivered outpace demand in recent years. The Denver area's vacancy rate reached a 16-year high of 7.6% late last year.

articles.title: Brooklyn Village site in Charlotte changes hands twice in two month span
articles.narrative: A key portion of the Brooklyn Village redevelopment in Charlotte, comprising 5.8 acres at 700 and 800 East Brooklyn Village Avenue, has been acquired by First and Early Partners for $24.3 million. This marks the second transaction for the property in two months, as Peachtree Group had previously acquired it from Peebles Corporation in May. The site was originally intended for the first phase of a $700 million redevelopment, including multifamily units and retail space, and its new owners have not yet disclosed their plans.

data_points.address: 700 and 800 East Brooklyn Village Avenue, Charlotte, NC
data_points.notable_features: Integral part of the Brooklyn Village redevelopment.
data_points.project_notes: The initial phase of the Brooklyn Village project was planned to include 496 market-rate multifamily units, 56 affordable units, and 20,000 square feet of retail space. Peachtree Group had greenlit $23.8 million in funds to Peebles Corporation in 2023 to secure the location and fund construction, and filed for foreclosure in early May before dismissing the action and transferring the deed.

articles.title: NYC’s top deals: Maspeth warehouse trades for $19M
articles.narrative: A 43,200-square-foot warehouse in Maspeth, Queens, was sold for $18.8 million to Grandview Portfolio Holdings LLC. The sellers were Patricia York and John P. Pantanelli. This transaction represents the priciest commercial deal recorded in New York City during the reporting period.

articles.title: “Freak accident”: Pfizer building developer denies risk of collapse
articles.narrative: The developer of the former Pfizer headquarters conversion in Midtown, MetroLoft, has addressed concerns following an emergency response at the construction site. Nathan Berman of MetroLoft stated that reports of an impending collapse were exaggerated, asserting the building was never at risk despite sagging upper floors and buckled support columns. He attributed the issue to added weight during construction, causing two specific columns to give way, and emphasized that the problem is fixable and will not significantly delay the project's 2027 completion.

data_points.address: 235 East 42nd Street, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Conversion of former office property into residential development.
data_points.project_notes: The project combines two former Pfizer headquarters buildings at 235 and 219 East 42nd Street into one residential development. Issues involved two buckled support columns and sagging floors in a 20x20 square foot corner of the building's northwest side.

articles.title: Policy Pro: HPD floats 421a rule change to keep more projects alive
articles.narrative: The New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) is proposing a rule change to the 421a tax abatement program, allowing developers to amend their affordability plans to qualify for a 2031 construction completion deadline extension. This aims to help projects that initially submitted non-compliant affordability workbooks to switch to eligible options, provided they had previously filed a letter of intent for an alternative. The change is a response to a 2024 housing deal that extended the 421a completion deadline by five years but required deeper affordability commitments. Additionally, the article notes that while the recently approved pied-à-terre tax will lead to new assessment methods for condos and co-ops, it is unlikely to directly spur comprehensive property tax reform in the near future, according to State Senator Brian Kavanagh.

articles.title: Meet the developers behind the Pfizer building conversion
articles.narrative: Metro Loft Management and David Werner are converting the former Pfizer headquarters at 235 East 42nd Street in Midtown East into approximately 1,500 rental units, making it the largest office-to-residential conversion in New York City. The project, which includes both luxury and affordable housing, recently secured a record $700 million construction loan from Madison Realty Capital. The development has faced several construction safety violations and incidents, including a recent fatality or injury notification failure and a worker fall.

data_points.address: 235 East 42nd Street, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Largest office-to-residential conversion in New York City, includes luxury rentals and affordable housing through the 467m tax abatement program.
data_points.project_notes: David Werner purchased the leasehold for 235 East 42nd Street for $407 million and 219 East 42nd Street for $142 million (initially with Alexandria Real Estate Equities, later buying out their stake). Nathan Berman acquired a minority stake in March 2024. The project has faced multiple construction safety violations and incidents, including a fatality/injury notification failure and a worker fall.

articles.title: NYCHA plumber’s $465K payday sparks probe into outside work
articles.narrative: A New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA) plumber supervisor is under investigation by the city's Department of Buildings for allegedly violating licensing rules related to his private plumbing businesses. The employee earned over $465,000 in the 2025 fiscal year, largely due to extensive overtime, while simultaneously being linked to more than 70 private plumbing jobs through two companies. The probe centers on whether his outside work was authorized after a promotion and his relationship with an unlicensed individual tied to one of his companies.

articles.title: Related Group’s Hollywood Live Local project draws suit from residents, nonprofit
articles.narrative: Hollywood residents and a newly formed nonprofit have filed a lawsuit against the City of Hollywood and an affiliate of Related Group, seeking to block a proposed beachfront luxury condo and community center project. The lawsuit claims the development violates a deed restriction requiring voter approval for long-term leases of public recreational land east of the Intracoastal Waterway and that the land must be used for public or municipal purposes. The developer plans to utilize Florida's Live Local Act to bypass rezoning, incorporating workforce housing units into the project.

data_points.notable_features: Proposed luxury condo and community center with 84 workforce housing units, located on a 4-acre site fronting a public beach.
data_points.project_notes: Related Group has a 99-year lease on the site, agreed to by city officials in 2022. The project is proceeding under Florida's Live Local Act, allowing the developer to bypass rezoning in exchange for providing below market-rate housing for those earning up to 120% of the area median income.

articles.title: AvalonBay buys city block in South Miami as investors get in position for multifamily bounceback
articles.narrative: AvalonBay Communities acquired a 1.2-acre full city block development site in South Miami for $22 million, where it plans to build a 16-story mixed-use project with 251 apartments and ground-floor retail. This transaction represents the highest per-unit price ever paid for a development site in South Miami. Separately, investor Adam Marcuvitz, through Midas Equities LLC, purchased two apartment properties in Fort Lauderdale for a combined $12.8 million, including a Flagler Village redevelopment site with 43 units and an 18-unit building in Harbordale. Marcuvitz intends to operate the Flagler Village property while awaiting improved development conditions, anticipating a multifamily market rebound as new supply deliveries taper off.

data_points.address: 5920 Sunset Drive to 5946 South Dixie Highway, South Miami, FL
data_points.notable_features: 16-story mixed-use development with ground-floor retail, pool, rooftop lounge, and 394 parking spaces. The site has 300 feet of waterfrontage and is one of the few remaining full-block development sites in downtown South Miami.
data_points.project_notes: The historic corner building at 5900 to 5904 Sunset Drive was not included in the sale. The Flagler Village site has redevelopment potential for 200 to 210 units. The Harbordale apartment building was built in 1973.

articles.financing: Flagler Village acquisition partially financed with a $4.4 million seller-carried mortgage. Harbordale acquisition partially financed through a $1.9 million seller-carried mortgage.
articles.market_intelligence: Multifamily deliveries are tapering off and development is slowing across South Florida after a post-pandemic building boom, according to CBRE.

articles.title: Nahla’s $1B Raleigh Miami Beach expansion proposal secures blessing from board despite height concerns
articles.narrative: Nahla Capital has secured a recommendation from the Miami Beach Planning Board to increase the floor area ratio for its proposed Raleigh Miami Beach project, a luxury condo and hotel development. This approval would add over 66,000 square feet to the project, allowing for two additional floors on the residential tower. The $1 billion development, which Nahla Capital acquired in October for $270 million, still requires final approval from the Miami Beach City Commission and the city’s historic preservation board. The project aims to revitalize the iconic Art Deco hotel, which has been closed since 2017, and will feature a Rosewood-branded hotel, luxury condominiums, and a private members' club.

data_points.notable_features: Rosewood-branded luxury condo and hotel project; iconic Art Deco design by L. Murray Dixon; includes a private members' club; located on "Billionaires' Beach."
data_points.project_notes: Nahla Capital acquired the 3-acre oceanfront assemblage in October for $270 million. The hotel has been closed since 2017. The project's height is 200 feet (approximately 17 stories).

articles.title: “You get what you pay for”: Fort Lauderdale will pursue $217M city hall project
articles.narrative: Fort Lauderdale commissioners have preliminarily approved a plan to develop a new $217.1 million city hall from the ground up, rather than retrofitting an existing building. The project, to be developed by FTL City Hall Partners LLC, will cost the city $15.8 million annually over 30 years. This decision follows a previous delay due to cost concerns and a subsequent reduction of approximately $50 million from the original design-build proposal, achieved by eliminating the developer's fee and equity stake. The city's former city hall was demolished after sustaining damage in a 2023 flood.

data_points.address: 100 North Andrews Avenue, Fort Lauderdale, FL
data_points.original_plan: 14-story, oval-shaped building with a sci-fi-reminiscent design for $268 million
data_points.project_notes: The city will pay $15.8 million annually for 30 years, totaling $474 million. The original proposal was $268 million, with annual payments of $24.1 million, totaling $723 million over 30 years. The lower price was achieved by scrapping a $12 million developer fee and 10 percent equity. The former city hall was demolished after flood damage in 2023.

articles.title: Waldorf Astoria set to take over W South Beach
articles.narrative: The W South Beach hotel is set to undergo a significant renovation and rebrand as a Waldorf Astoria property, with an expected reopening in winter 2027. The project, led by owners Reuben Brothers, will include a redesign of 348 oceanfront guest suites, a new lobby, upgraded dining venues, and an enhanced spa and pool deck. The change in branding from Marriott's W to Waldorf Astoria will result in the termination of over 300 employees, though the owners anticipate creating new employment opportunities post-renovation. This renovation is part of Reuben Brothers' expanding hospitality portfolio in South Florida.

data_points.notable_features: Oceanfront property with 48,000-square-foot pool deck and private cabanas.
data_points.project_notes: The hotel portion will close for renovations on August 20. The property was previously acquired for over $400 million in 2024. Upgrade plans filed with the Miami Beach Historic Preservation Board were partially approved in April, excluding a restaurant, valet canopy, and nightclub renovation, leading the company to withdraw and refile the application.

articles.title: Frank Gehry-designed “Icehenge” desk up for auction in Chicago
articles.narrative: A unique green-tinted glass desk, known as "Icehenge" and designed by the late architect Frank Gehry, is being offered for auction by Freeman Auctioneers. The 7-ton, 16-piece desk was originally created for the Inland Steel Building in Downtown Chicago, where Gehry also held a small ownership stake for a period. The auction house estimates the desk will fetch between $100,000 and $200,000, with a starting bid of $50,000.

data_points.notable_features: The desk is a 7-ton, 16-piece green-tinted glass sculpture, with its tallest column approximately six feet tall, designed by Frank Gehry and nicknamed "Icehenge".

articles.title: Glencoe mansion seeks $7M in bid to crack off-lakefront pricing record
articles.narrative: A luxury single-family home in Glencoe, IL, located two blocks from Glencoe Beach, has been listed for sale at $6.95 million. The 10,000-square-foot residence, built in 2019, features six bedrooms and nine bathrooms. The asking price aims to set a new record for a non-lakefront home in the affluent North Shore suburb, reflecting its high-quality construction, design, and amenities.

data_points.notable_features: Located two blocks from Glencoe Beach, this luxury home features six bedrooms and nine bathrooms.
data_points.project_notes: The property was previously acquired for $3.7 million in March 2020.

articles.title: Former professional golf coach Hank Haney selling home in Glencoe
articles.narrative: Former professional golf coach Hank Haney has listed his Glencoe residence for $4.3 million. Haney and his wife purchased the 8,400-square-foot home in January 2024 for approximately $3.8 million. The property, built in 2022, features a cabana house, outdoor kitchen, and a pool, and is situated on just under a half-acre.

data_points.notable_features: Features a cabana house with a deck, an outdoor kitchen, and a pool.
data_points.project_notes: Previously acquired in January 2024 for approximately $3.8 million.

articles.title: Tesla leases 683K sf speculative industrial building amid Central Texas expansion spree
articles.narrative: Tesla has leased a 682,000-square-foot speculative industrial building within the Austin Hills Commerce Center, a project being developed by Sansone Group and Principal Asset Management. This lease represents the second phase of the development, which is expected to be completed by January 2027. The transaction underscores the significant demand for large industrial spaces in the Austin market, as Tesla continues its rapid expansion in Central Texas.
articles.market_intelligence: There are at least a dozen speculative industrial buildings spanning upwards of 400,000 square feet in various stages of development across the Austin area. Tesla currently leases 2.2 million square feet and owns over 10 million square feet of space around Austin.

articles.title: Toyota commits to San Antonio plant expansion with $4 billion plan
articles.narrative: Toyota is investing $3.6 billion to significantly expand its manufacturing presence in San Antonio, TX, by 2030. The plan includes a second 2.5 million-square-foot vehicle assembly line for Tacoma pickup truck production, consolidating operations from a previous location. This expansion, supported by $178 million in local tax incentives and a $20 million state grant, is projected to generate a $3.2 billion economic impact during construction and create approximately 6,000 jobs.

data_points.address: 1 Lone Star Pass, San Antonio, TX
data_points.notable_features: Expansion includes a second vehicle assembly line for Tacoma pickup truck production.
data_points.project_notes: The 2.5 million-square-foot facility will be built on Toyota's existing 2,000-acre campus. San Antonio City Council and Bexar County commissioners approved $178 million in tax incentives. The Texas Enterprise Fund provided a $20 million grant. Toyota is also planning a 32,000-square-foot office building at the campus, adding $18.2 million to its investment.

articles.title: Lift Partners picks up trio of Santa Clara industrial buildings for nearly $26M
articles.narrative: Lift Partners has acquired a three-building industrial property in Santa Clara, CA, for approximately $25.8 million from an affiliate of Vantage Data Centers. The 7-acre site, located near San Jose Mineta International Airport, includes a mix of warehouse and service center space. The property's heavy industrial zoning and size make it a notable asset in the region, with potential for significant new development.

data_points.notable_features: Heavy industrial zoning; located one block west of San Jose Mineta International Airport.
data_points.project_notes: The site was previously proposed for a 468,000-square-foot data center by the seller, but the application was withdrawn. The property can accommodate up to 148,635 square feet of new development.

articles.market_intelligence: Silicon Valley is a hub for industrial investment in the Bay Area. Recent transactions include Clarion Partners' $132.3 million acquisition of a 267,100-square-foot industrial building in Fremont, Redco Development's $42 million purchase of a 13-acre former UPS facility in Sunnyvale for redevelopment into a 265,000-square-foot industrial building, and Morgan Stanley Investment Management's $110.3 million acquisition of a two-building, 290,000-square-foot manufacturing property in Fremont.

articles.title: SF brokers have a new question for homebuyers: Got an extra million?
articles.narrative: San Francisco's luxury housing market is experiencing unprecedented competition, with 144 homes selling for at least $1 million over asking price in the first half of 2026, a significant increase from previous years. This trend is partly driven by a deliberate pricing strategy where homes are listed low to ignite bidding wars, capitalizing on high demand and scarce inventory. While the booming AI industry and upcoming IPOs are often cited, market analysts suggest the surge is more closely tied to the broader stock market's record highs, which translates into liquid wealth for tech employees in the region.
articles.market_intelligence: San Francisco is the only housing market west of the Mississippi River with more buyers than sellers, with buyers outstripping sellers by 14% in May. In contrast, Oakland saw sellers outnumber buyers by over 30%, and Los Angeles by 56%.

articles.title: Sunset Development taps for Bishop Ranch resi
Santa Clara County property values hit record high $760B
articles.narrative: Santa Clara County's taxable property values reached a record $760.1 billion for the 2026-27 fiscal year, marking a 4.7% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by changes in ownership, particularly residential sales, which contributed $16.9 billion, and inflation adjustments adding $14 billion. New construction also played a role, contributing $4.9 billion, though several major development projects remain delayed. The county faces challenges from a lagging office market, with vacancy rates near 20% and a significant volume of commercial property assessment appeals that could impact future tax revenues.

articles.title: Chase Bank Branch Garners Manhattan’s Sixth-Highest Price Per Square Foot Since 2023
articles.narrative: SURMOUNT, a net lease real estate advisory and investment platform, has completed the $13 million sale of a Chase Bank branch located at 1295 Madison Ave. in Manhattan's Carnegie Hill neighborhood. The 3,000-square-foot ground-floor retail property traded at a 4.74% cap rate, achieving $4,300 per square foot. This price per square foot ranks as the sixth highest for a retail sale in Manhattan since 2023, underscoring the asset's prime location and the strong demand for trophy retail properties in the market.

data_points.address: 1295 Madison Ave, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Ground-floor bank branch located in the Carnegie Hill neighborhood.
data_points.project_notes: The property was previously acquired by the seller in 2024.

articles.market_intelligence: The sale price per square foot of $4,300 ranks as the sixth highest for a retail sale in Manhattan since 2023.

articles.title: Marcus & Millichap Brokers Self-Storage Property Deal in Chicago
articles.narrative: Marcus & Millichap has brokered the sale of a newly constructed Public Storage facility in Chicago, Illinois. The 916-unit, climate-controlled self-storage property was completed in 2024 and is strategically located in a densely populated area with high visibility. The transaction highlights Chicago's robust self-storage market, driven by constrained new supply and strong rental rates, which continues to attract investors seeking high-quality assets.

data_points.notable_features: Climate-controlled units, institutional-quality facility, strong visibility along North Kedzie Avenue, situated in a densely populated area with a predominantly renter-occupied housing base.

articles.market_intelligence: Chicago is identified as one of the strongest self-storage rental rate markets due to above-average development complexity constraining new supply.

articles.title: Milhaus Receives Approval to Develop Kansas City Affordable Apartments
articles.narrative: Milhaus has secured Low-Income Housing Tax Credits from the Missouri Housing Development Commission, along with a tax abatement and Housing Trust Fund allocation, to develop the Linwood & Troost Apartments in Kansas City. This project will transform two vacant lots into a 194-unit, 100% affordable residential community across two four-story buildings. This marks Milhaus's inaugural Low-Income Housing Tax Credit development in the Kansas City market.

data_points.notable_features: 100% affordable residential development located on the Troost MAX transit corridor with transit-supportive infrastructure.
data_points.project_notes: Funding includes 4% federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, a tax abatement from Kansas City’s Planned Industrial Expansion Authority, and $1.5 million from the Kansas City Housing Trust Fund. Construction is expected to begin by the end of 2026.

articles.title: Targus Relocates Headquarters to BGO-Owned Business Park
articles.narrative: Targus, a global leader in laptop cases and mobile computing accessories, has signed an 84,041-square-foot industrial lease at Anaheim Concourse, relocating its corporate headquarters to a newly constructed Class A facility. The move represents a strategic decision to upgrade to a modern building with enhanced functionality and a prime location, supporting the company's long-term growth while maintaining connectivity to its workforce and customer base. The transaction highlights the ongoing trend of occupiers prioritizing high-quality facilities in established infill markets.

data_points.notable_features: Class A facility with 32-foot clear heights, an ESFR sprinkler system, a secured truck court, and direct access to major freeway networks.

articles.title: Joseph Kavanagh Co. Completes Sale of HQ, Manufacturing Facility
articles.narrative: Joseph Kavanagh Co. has sold its 19,000-square-foot corporate headquarters and manufacturing facility in Dundalk, Maryland, to Titan Steel Corporation for $2.3 million. The property, which includes office, industrial, and warehouse space, is situated on a 2.27-acre site with excellent access to major transportation routes.

data_points.notable_features: Features 14- to 16.5-foot ceilings, two drive-in loading docks, approximately 2,500 square feet of office space, and a fenced outdoor storage yard. The site fronts Interstate 696 and is located near Interstate 95 and the Dundalk Marine Terminal.

articles.title: World Cup Delivers Assist For U.S. Hotels, But Not At Super Bowl Scale
articles.narrative: The 2026 FIFA World Cup has provided a significant boost to the U.S. hotel industry, though not quite reaching the "Super Bowl-size" economic impact initially projected by tournament organizers. Early returns show strong but not exceptional revenue per available room (RevPAR) and average daily rate (ADR) increases, driven by shorter-term stays rather than the anticipated weeklong visits. While host markets experienced an 18.7% year-over-year RevPAR increase during the group stage, the overall U.S. hotel industry achieved record highs for RevPAR and ADR in late June, with match days showing a 25.8% RevPAR increase. Short-term rentals also saw rate increases, particularly on game days, and industry experts anticipate further premiums as the tournament progresses into later stages, especially with popular teams advancing.

articles.title: Prince William County Board Rejects Plan For 1,940-Acre Data Center Hub
articles.narrative: The Prince William County Board of Supervisors unanimously rejected a comprehensive plan amendment for the proposed Dulles South Innovation Center, a 1,940-acre data center hub in Gainesville. The decision prevents the rezoning of land from agriculture, forestry, and mixed-use to industrial, which would have allowed for up to 42M SF of data center space. This rejection follows significant public debate over environmental concerns, infrastructure strain, and the preservation of the area's rural character, marking another setback for large-scale data center development in the county.

data_points.notable_features: Proposed data center hub adjacent to Loudoun County and Fairfax County boundaries.
data_points.project_notes: The county's board of supervisors declined to initiate a comprehensive plan amendment, which was an early step in the approval process. The proposal was submitted by Sanders Lane Assemblage I LLC, representing over 200 homeowners who had agreed to sell their properties for the project.

articles.title: Brookfield JV Buys Site For 6,500-Unit Project In Boston Suburbs
articles.narrative: A joint venture between Brookfield Properties and New England Development has acquired a significant portion of the former South Weymouth Naval Air Station site for $65 million. The developers plan a massive mixed-use project, including 6,500 housing units and 2 million square feet of commercial space, making it the largest residential and commercial development in Massachusetts. This acquisition marks a major milestone for the long-stalled redevelopment of the 1,400-acre site, with infrastructure improvements expected to begin this fall.

data_points.notable_features: Former naval air base site, preserving over 880 acres for open space and wildlife habitat.
data_points.project_notes: The site was previously controlled by Washington Capital Management after LStar Ventures' redevelopment efforts stalled. The Southfield Redevelopment Authority selected the Brookfield and New England Development venture as the new master developer in early 2020. New zoning guidelines were approved in November 2025. Weymouth received a $32.5M state grant for infrastructure improvements.

articles.title: Blackstone Eyes £6B Indurent Exit As Logistics M&A Heats Up
articles.narrative: Blackstone is exploring a potential sale or London listing for Indurent, its UK industrial and logistics platform, which could be valued at approximately £6 billion. Indurent was formed in February 2024 through the merger of Industrials REIT and St Modwen Logistics, and has since expanded with £2 billion in acquisitions and developments. Separately, Prologis is attempting a £12.6 billion all-stock takeover of Segro, the UK's largest publicly traded property company, an offer that Segro's board has rejected as undervalued, citing market dislocation and the company's embedded growth potential. Segro has also recently formed a joint venture with PSP to develop three major UK logistics parks.

data_points.project_notes: Indurent was created by Blackstone in February 2024 by merging Industrials REIT and St Modwen Logistics. The company has since undertaken £2 billion in acquisitions and developments. Any deal is likely at least 18 months away.

articles.title: Nscale Secures $900M For Data Center Expansion
articles.narrative: Nscale, an AI infrastructure firm, has secured a $900 million line of credit to accelerate the construction of its global data center portfolio across the U.S., Europe, and Asia. This financing will provide the necessary liquidity for the company's rapid expansion, reflecting strong investor confidence in its strategic direction and growth prospects within the burgeoning AI infrastructure market. The company's CEO highlighted that this facility enhances their flexibility to build the essential infrastructure required by major technology companies for AI development and scaling.
articles.market_intelligence: Neoclouds, which provide on-demand access to GPU computing for AI, are the fastest-growing data center segment, experiencing 223% year-over-year revenue growth in Q4 2025.
